title: Bucketized KV recycler and hotspot-aware page allocator to reduce fragmentation and spill spikes
author: Asha Menon
description:
Context: We see recurring tail-node memory pressure during mixed tenant workloads that creates short-lived spill spikes and elevated fragmentation. Root causes: heterogeneous object sizes in the KV cache, cross-tenant allocation churn, and the allocator's coarse-grained free-list causing long-lived tiny fragments. Motivation: reduce spill frequency and smooth spillback latency while preserving median token-generation latency.

Summary of change: Introduce a bucketized recycler for KV allocations plus a lightweight hotspot-aware page allocator that prefers colocating same-size live objects and relaxes coalescing rules for hot pages. The recycler maintains size-segregated freelists with per-tenant buckets; the page allocator tracks page hotness via a compact approximate counter and avoids immediate page reclamation for hot pages, deferring compaction to a background compactor that runs with IO/CPU caps. This PR also adds a small scheduling hint in the serving runtime that batches reclamations during low-latency windows (continuous-batcher cooperation).

What I changed (high level): sizes: added two new packages and modified allocator paths. Behavior: tenant-aware freelists, per-bucket deferred-compaction flags, page hotness counter, background compactor with rate limiter, small changes to batcher to delay reclaim flushes.

Commits (high level):
- a1f4b2a: initial bucketized recycler implementation and tests
- b2d8c9f: hotspot counter and page allocator integration + microbenchmarks
- c3e5f77: background compactor and rate limiter + e2e test harness updates
- d4f6a01: scheduling hint in continuous-batcher + metrics and docs
- e5a7b8c: address review feedback, optimize freelist locks, CI fixes

Files touched (high level): pkg/kv/cache/recycler.go, pkg/kv/cache/recycler_test.go, pkg/kv/allocator/page_hotspots.go, pkg/kv/allocator/allocator_integration.go, runtime/batcher/reclaim_hints.go, runtime/batcher/reclaim_integration_test.go, tooling/benchmarks/kv_fragmentation/bench_runner.go, docs/notes/kv-recycler-design.md, telemetry/metrics/kv_hotspot.metrics.yml, third_party/README.md

Files changed count: 12, Additions: 842, Deletions: 276.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for bucket lifecycle and hotspot counters. Bench harness added to reproduce fragmentation scenarios. CI summary: initial CI run failed one flaky integration test (reclaim_integration_test) due to timing assumption; adjusted test to use retry window and re-ran. Final CI: all checks pass (unit/integration/bench).

Performance results (internal cluster, synthetic mixed-tenancy workload):
- Fragmentation score (measured by randomized probe): median down 12%, 95th down 28%
- Spill events per hour: 30% reduction under spikey workloads (same aggregate QPS)
- Tail spill latency (time to spill resolution): p95 reduced from 420ms -> 310ms
- Median generation latency: neutral (+1% within noise)
- Background compaction CPU: average 2.4% host CPU during steady-state (configurable)

Rollout plan: staged rollout on Dedicated candidates. Feature gated behind kv.bucket_recycler and kv.hotspot_allocator flags. Start with canary subset of tenants for 48h, validate spill counts and memory overhead, then expand. There is a safe fallback path: toggling the feature flags disables bucketized freelists and reverts to previous allocator.

Related work and references: ENG-2147 (bucketized allocator exploration), ENG-2201 (spill stabilization), previous KV compaction PRs were focused on eviction heuristics; this PR focuses upstream in the allocator to reduce fragmentation at allocation time.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to concurrency around bucket freelist locks (fine-grained sharding), and the trade-offs in the hotspot counter decay window. I left knobs as config in pkg/kv/allocator/config.go.

release_notes: Introduces bucketized KV recycler and hotspot-aware page allocator that reduce fragmentation and spikey spill events. Feature gated: kv.bucket_recycler and kv.hotspot_allocator. Rollout plan included; safe rollback via feature flags.
review_summary: Started as design + implementation by Asha. Reviewers requested lock reduction and clearer metrics. After two rounds author addressed sharding contention, added bench harness, and adjusted compactor rate limiter. Approved by Lucas and Nina. Diego requested observability tweak which was included.
discussion:
Lucas Park: Nice end-to-end, two high-level asks: (1) can we reduce contention on freelist when a tenant has many small allocations? (2) add a prometheus metric for hotpage eviction deferrals.
Asha Menon: for (1) added bucket sharding and per-tenant bucket maps to reduce lock span; microbench shows 18% lower lock hold time. For (2) added kv_hotpage_deferred_total and kv_hotpage_deferred_seconds in telemetry.
Nina Gupta: integration test flaked once due to timing; prefer test to use adaptive wait instead of fixed sleep.
Asha Menon: updated reclaim_integration_test to use retry with backoff.
Diego Alvarez: can compactor interfere with other background IO? Suggests rate limiter with CPU cap and backpressure signal.
Asha Menon: implemented token-bucket rate limiter that observes host CPU and queues compaction when IO busy; documented knobs.
CI Bot: Unit tests passed. Integration tests failed on first run (flaky reclaim test). Re-run: all green.
QA: Bench harness reproduces fragmentation scenario; results attached in bench_runner output.
notes: Config knobs: kv.bucket_recycler.enabled, kv.bucket_recycler.shard_count, kv.hotspot_allocator.decay_window_ms, kv.hotspot_compactor.max_cpu_pct. Default safe settings chosen for Dedicated clusters.
